steps.name: Inam
steps.text: No need to be shy, Tomimi. It looks great on you.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: R-Really?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Ehehe, I loved this swimsuit the moment I laid eyes on it. It's exactly my style!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: The tailors here sure are something. They managed to custom-make something to fit your figure so quickly.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: I-is there something wrong with my figure? I've been working out a lot harder!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Don't worry. You look super cute.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Phew, that's good then. I don't want people making fun of my tail getting thicker again... Inam, you're not going to pick out a swimsuit?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I'm good. I'm more interested in the buckethead that was helping out the tailor just now.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Durin technology...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That's some crazy good stuff!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I've never had liquor this good before!

steps.name: Tipsy Durin
steps.text: Cheers, brother! Let's drink to your health!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: A toast to our health! Long live Old Karl Mead!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Hey, Tomimi, about that Elysium guy... Is he actually reliable?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Eh? He's there for us, when the chips are down...

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Usually!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Now that you mention it, there are Durin operators at Rhodes Island, but they seem to never talk about where they came from.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Do you think the Durins might be hiding something?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: No, I think they just don't care a whole lot. They always seem a lot more concerned about what's on the menu in the canteen.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I never thought we'd get the opportunity to explore an underground Durin city.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Yeah. This might be a great opportunity to spread Gavial's name to the Durin people as well...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You didn't drag Gavial, Zumama, and Kemar with you on vacation this time?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Kemar said she wanted to practice boxing with Blaze. Gavial and Zumama went on a mission and haven't come back yet.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Gavial's been working way too hard recently, and that worries me!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: I really wish she wouldn't push herself so much...

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: I wrote them a letter before I left, telling what you learned from Mr. Stitch, as well as what he told us.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: They could've taken the opportunity to go back to Acahualla for a break...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: The three of you went and made me Great Chief without a second thought, and it's about time you all came back to see what I've gotten done.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: By the way, while you were at Rhodes Island, did anybody find this Elysium guy a little annoying?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Waheeeey, it's a completely different experience!

steps.name: Piss-Drunk Durin
steps.text: You, tall guy, I saw you hanging out with those mead boys just now. Listen up, that stuff's for kids!

steps.name: Piss-Drunk Durin
steps.text: If you want the REAL good booze, turn your eyes toward our No. 7 Whiskey. Here, cheers.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Cheers!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: This aroma... it's like the rainforest after a thunderstorm, the smell of moss in an underground cave!

steps.name: Piss-Drunk Durin
steps.text: Oh. Sorry, that's just the wood cup getting a little moldy.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: He seems to be enjoying himself.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Oh, Inam, you still haven't told me about how you met Mr. Stitch.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Hm... It's a bit of a long story.

steps.name: Excited Archosauria
steps.text: Great Chief, the big things you brought with you last time were really stimulating! Just standing in front of them kept me up for days!

steps.name: Excited Archosauria
steps.text: My wife's been nagging me day in and day out about how these things are gonna snatch away my soul or something!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: We're talking about those heaps of junk from Columbia, right? Are those metal choppers that big of a deal?

steps.name: Excited Archosauria
steps.text: You bet they are! A legendary construction device, those things are, a machine of machines! Have you ever felt the joy of watching those things work right in front of you? My heart's never pounded so hard, not even when I first met my wife!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Huh... Guess I'll have someone stop by to put shock absorbers on your chopper one of these days.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Tomimi's going to be back in a few days, so we've got to get ready to pick her up.

steps.name: No Longer Excited Archosauria
steps.text: Picking up Tomimi? I can imagine how much work that's going to take.

steps.name: Groaning Archosauria
steps.text: It's probably about as bad as getting beaten up by a metal chopper.

steps.name: No Longer Excited Archosauria
steps.text: Who knows how many trinkets and doodads she'll bring back with her? Do you remember how many men we needed to grab all her stuff last time?

steps.name: No Longer Excited Archosauria
steps.text: At first, I thought it was a whole caravan!

steps.name: Groaning Archosauria
steps.text: Tomimi's always been like that, ever since she was little. Always hoarding whatever junk she gets her hands on...

steps.name: Groaning Archosauria
steps.text: Don't you think it's gotten worse since she went to Rhodes Island?

steps.name: No Longer Excited Archosauria
steps.text: I have no idea why she had to lug back that plate of sheet metal. The one Gavial put a hole through.

steps.name: Groaning Archosauria
steps.text: I heard she couldn't find a place to put it in her place at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Wait, who's that up ahead?
Call me mad, signing up for this kind of abuse. First it was those topsy-turvy caves, now it's this godforsaken place.
But that old man Eartheart drives me up the wall. Just clogs up the doorway and nags you all day... Gah, damn these stupid vines! And that accursed sunlight!
I've always said artificial lighting is much better than this crap!
I'm so thirsty... And tired.
I can't fathom why the Master would leave Zeruertza. Is he a masochist or something?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: A little kid?

steps.name: A little kid?
steps.text: Who are you calling a kid? You're the kid!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Huh, you've got a pretty funny accent. Who taught you?

steps.name: A little kid?
steps.text: I taught myself. Got a problem with that?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Kids ought to mind their manners and be patient with strangers.

steps.name: Archosauria
steps.text: What a funny-looking fella. Kind of familiar, though, anyone like this been around Acahualla? Did someone's kid go missing?

steps.name: Archosauria
steps.text: Not a thick-tail, or a thin-tail...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Not a Liberi, or a Phidia either. Wait, hold on, could you be...?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: A Durin?

steps.name: Archosauria
steps.text: What's a Durin? Can you eat it?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I've only read about them in magazines, but apparently Durins are a mysterious race of people who live underground.

steps.name: Archosauria
steps.text: You mean a metal crab?

steps.name: Maybe a Metal Crab?
steps.text: No, you're the metal crab! Wanna fight?!

steps.name: Archosauria
steps.text: Oh, I remember now! There was an article in 'Stranger Things' a few years ago about how the Durins were really good at making alcohol! That's something metal crabs can't do.

steps.name: Archosauria
steps.text: At best, metal crabs might get drunk off of eating fermented fruits.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: They also don't live underground. They just cover themselves with dirt.

steps.name: Not a Metal Crab
steps.text: That's not what matters!

steps.name: Not a Metal Crab
steps.text: *sigh*... I knew it. You surface-dwellers are just a bunch of short-sighted egomaniacs who keep running their mouths despite not knowing anything.

steps.name: Not a Metal Crab
steps.text: You people even make Durins look smart.

steps.name: Not a Metal Crab
steps.text: Gah, beyond all that though, your aesthetic sensibilities are compelte trash.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Hey, little Durin, I'll have you know— I'm wearing Sargon's chicest styles.

steps.name: Pint-Sized Durin
steps.text: If that's your idea of 'chic,' then it's all the proof I need that everyone up here has trash taste. What is the point in going along with aesthetic merit determined by someone else? You might as well be a lowly pleb.

steps.name: Archosauria
steps.text: Great Chief, I think this kid might have a few screws loose. Need me to fix him up?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: He's still got a long life ahead of him. Let him be.

steps.name: Pint-Sized Durin
steps.text: I matured a long time ago, thank you very much!

steps.name: Mature Durin
steps.text: Ugh... Why am I even wasting time talking to these ignoramuses? Farewell.

steps.name: Archosauria
steps.text: Oh. There he goes.

steps.name: Archosauria
steps.text: Hmm? He stopped again?

steps.name: Mature Durin
steps.text: Uhh...

steps.name: Mature Durin
steps.text: Ahem... Uhh, if I may ask a small favor, surface-dwellers...

steps.name: Mature Durin
steps.text: Can I have some water?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: So, the rest is pretty much what you wrote in the letter? He said that a Durin city is in trouble and needs our help?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: At least, that's what Stitch said at the time.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Take a good look around us! How could this beautiful city possibly...?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: *hic*! How could there possibly be any trouble?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Well, uhh, the drinks here being way too good can be troublesome. Might end up under the table if you're not careful, but that would NEVER happen to me. Cheers!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: This is probably that unsociable little rascal's roundabout way of inviting us to see his beautiful home, and I can totally understand that sentiment.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Not everyone's brain is fried like yours, Elysium.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Stitch stayed with us for a month, and one day, he was pestering a group of Archosauria building a train.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: He said, uh, 'You folks are good enough! These bits of iron and copper you've soldered together might be able to help me! Want to come down to Zeruertza to have a look?'

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: So then you–– Brother, mind topping me off? I'll finish yours––

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: So, you went along with it?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Though Stitch was definitely exaggerating the scope of the crisis, I... was actually curious to see if there's any business to be done with our underground neighbors.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Good idea!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: If Acahualla ever wants to escape its savage, brutish state, it'll need every opportunity it can get. I heard the Durins are exceptional at smelting and smithing. If we could do them a favor, we might be able to get a thing or two in return...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You folks won't have to get all excited over a few bits of scrap metal anymore.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Inam... I didn't expect you to be such an upstanding Great Chief! I thought you'd just blow all your money in the city every day.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You brat. Is that how you think of me?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: If Acahualla wants to develop, the most important thing it needs is money. Doesn't matter if it's Sargonian coins, Columbian bills, or Victorian pounds. We need them all.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: But with Acahualla's current manufacturing output – some shoddy handmade products, a bit of unrefined ore, we barely have enough money for people to live decently, let alone think about getting rich.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Luckily, you don't have to worry about how the city defines 'living decently.'

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: That said, there's a difference between money and wealth. Sitting on a stack of money doesn't accomplish anything, but once you get it into circulation, then it becomes 'wealth.'

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Acahualla is already on the up and up. But to become even better, it needs opportunity.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: For example, a technological partnership with the Durins.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Hmm, this is a bit beyond me... All I know is, whenever I run into a problem, I throw some Arts at it! If that doesn't work, I can always whack it with my staff!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: That's the 'Gavial's Will' way of life!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Hahaha! Even after working with Rhodes Island for so long, you still can't leave your roots behind, huh?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: But, uhh, the best that I can do is some tinkering around the edges. For Acahualla to truly develop, we still need a 'leader.'

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: But Inam, aren't you already the Great Chief?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: A leader is someone who can truly unite the Tiacauh. Am I gonna do that? A little too troublesome for me.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I'd rather go shopping in the city.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I like the way you think! I'm quite fond of shopping myself, but nothing beats the great outdoors, *hic*!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: By the way, I haven't seen our little motor-mouthed friend for quite some time. Did he sneak off somewhere?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Seems like it...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I'd assume he went to set something up?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Oh, right, but since we're right in front of the big water slide... It wouldn't hurt to enjoy our vacation first, right?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: I, I think the Yanese Operators at Rhodes Island have a saying for this! It goes something like... uhh, 'the host plans, and the guests follow'?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: I think that means... Since the host isn't here, we can do whatever we want.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: *hic*! Well said! I'll drink again to that pearl of wisdom!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Race you to the foot of the slide, my friends!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Elysium really is getting used to the Durin lifestyle a bit too quickly...

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: *pant* *pant*... Finally shook off that rabble of drunkards.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: That's why I can't stand these soulless Durins! What are these idiots wasting their precious lives on?!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I've only been away for a month, and Zeruertza's already turned into a terrible eyesore. Dammit! I never should've come back!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: And as for those stupid surface-dwellers... Gah, as long as they can build me a railway bridge that won't collapse, I suppose I can compromise my standards a bit more.

steps.name: Elderly Durin
steps.text: Stitch? You really came back to us! Word was going around about a teetotaler Durin wandering Zeruertza. I knew it had to be you!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Edge Eartheart... You're never going to leave me alone, are you?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Where have you been all this time? I was running all over looking for you. I wore out my old bones searching around that cave-in!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Your old bones are harder than rock. I, on the other hand, nearly died.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Don't tell me, you... went to the surface?!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: What, you got a problem?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I can't believe you did that, Stitch.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: You, you're too gutsy for your own good. I never imagined you'd...

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Actually manage to do something useful! Hurry, let me see what fancy goodies you brought back!

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: The network of caves above the lift is way too hard to navigate, and I have no clue where my map went. Nobody's been up there in years!

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: You remembered to bring me a souvenir, right? Or maybe some exotic ore specimens? Some fermentable surface plants? The latest issue of 'Stranger Things'?! The ones they have at the library are all out-of-date.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: No, uhh, how should I put this...?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I brought a few people back.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: 'Thus, she decided...'

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: 'She decided on Old Karl Mead!'

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: Ugh, that's not good enough. Maybe the product placement should come a bit earlier? Let me revise that a bit...

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: 'Cheaper than cheap. Crazier than crazy!'

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: 'If you need a place to cut loose, have a great time, and, of course, enjoy a sip of some soul-soothing mead—'

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: 'Look no further than Zeruertza and our famed Old Karl Mead!'

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: Good. Concise, straightforward, and lavish in praise. The client should be satisfied with this. Hopefully.
